output:
Short answer
- Pick an LED task/desk lamp with high delivered lumens, high efficacy (lm/W), good color rendering (CRI), and dimming/controls. From the catalog I found one candidate, the "Harbor Task Lamp" — I can check its full specs if you want, but my memory only lists its name (no technical details or source).

Why an LED task lamp is the best single upgrade
- LEDs use far less electricity than incandescent/halogen for the same light output and last much longer, so they lower operating and replacement costs.
- Good task lighting (focused, adjustable) lets you use lower ambient lighting for the whole office, saving energy building-wide.

Recommended target specs and why they matter
- Light output (lumens): ~600–1,200 lm for typical desk work. This gives bright, even task illumination without needing very high ambient levels.
- Efficacy: >=80 lm/W (higher is better). This tells you how energy-efficient the lamp actually is.
- Color rendering (CRI): >=80 for general office work; >=90 if accurate color is important (graphics, design).
- Correlated color temperature (CCT): 3000–4000 K is usually best for offices (3000K = warmer; 4000K = neutral/cooler).
- Dimmable: saves energy and improves comfort when full output isn’t needed.
- Adjustable arm/head and precise beam control: reduces wasted light and glare.
- Certifications: ENERGY STAR or DLC listing if you want verified efficiency/performance.
- Controls: occupancy sensor or programmable timers can reduce on-time in shared spaces.
- Flicker and strobe spec (if provided): low flicker (<5–10% or specified as low-flicker) helps reduce eyestrain for sensitive users.

Evidence I used and what needs verification
- Evidence available from memory: the catalog contains entries labeled desk lamp, adjustable desk lamps, task lamps, lighting products, and one named Harbor Task Lamp. I do not have technical specs, images, or provenance for any of these items in memory.
- Claims that require verification before purchase:
  - Harbor Task Lamp: I have only the name in memory — verify wattage, lumens, CRI, CCT, efficacy (lm/W), dimmability, adjustability, mounting options, warranty, price, and any ENERGY STAR/DLC certification.
  - Any numerical energy-saving claims (e.g., "saves X% vs incandescent"): those depend on the lamp’s actual wattage and your current lamps — we must compare real specs and usage hours.
  - Lifetime estimates and maintenance savings should be checked against manufacturer lifetime (L70 hours) and warranty information.

If you want, I can:
1) Pull full specs and provenance for the Harbor Task Lamp from the product catalog and compare it to 2–3 alternative ENERGY STAR/DLC-listed LED task lamps; or
2) Recommend specific models from known manufacturers (BenQ, Lumiy, TaoTronics, FLOS, etc.) with verified specs; or
3) Help you choose the best spec targets for your office if you tell me typical desk size, current lamp type, budget, and whether you prefer warmer or cooler light.

Which would you prefer me to do next?
